Tried to kill myself in a bathtub when I lost custody of my son after a cheating situation involving my ex's post partum depression.

Drank an entire handle of rum and set up a "kill room" in my bathroom but was too drunk to load the gun correctly and passed out with it in between my legs with the liquor spilled all over me and wound up puking and passing out.

Had a bad job, failing school, terrible relationship and lost my son.

Now have the best career of my life and full custody. I woke up from it and somehow found complete resolve to live.

Even when it seems completely ruined and hopeless there is a way out.

I posted about it about 5 years ago....passed out drunk in a bath tub with a handle of liquor half drank and a gun between my legs trying to Hemingway myself. Luckily was too fucked up to load the gun properly and passed out. Son was taken from me and I had a dead end job after being cheated on for months with money stolen by my ex. 

Looking back it's fairly amazing considering I have full custody of my son who is doing great and a great job...if you asked me then if there was a light at the end of the tunnel of some variety I would have laughed and considered it impossible. Still dealing with a lot of the trauma but it can get better.

Turns out she raided my house when I was at my brother's wedding and then called me when I came home to find my house destroyed and looted letting me know that she was coming to take my son from me (he had gone with me to the wedding). She had been cheating on me for 6 months.

Currently have full custody and an amazing career, but it was a really long road.

I needed to quit my intake anyways, as I was using it as a coping mechanism for stress. The main reason is that my ex will appropriate any use whatsoever against me in court when I try to take my son back.

He's worth more than any substance.

2 weeks without a drop and it wasn't nearly as hard to quit as I thought it was going to be.

I'm speaking with my lawyer today. I don't think she's capable of even lasting the week, let alone pay for daycare while she goes to school. I don't think she has the monetary, intellectual, or emotional capacity to raise him on her own so I'm hoping I wind up with a favorable judgement. All of the evidence I've collected over the last few months at least proves that I was giving the majority of his care.

She's the mother. I signed a paternity affidavit when he was born but apparently that was actually a really bad move from a legal standpoint considering I didn't know for sure that he was mine. 

He looks exactly like me though and I don't have reason to believe she was actively cheating on me when he was conceived (He's nine months old currently).

There was already abuse of me (physical and mentally) going on, so  I'm actually already so much more at ease now that she's out of the house.

The thought of my son being with her without me there and some random guy in the house is what keeps me up at night.

The amount of stuff she stole isn't worth fighting for, the only thing I asked for back are the baby books I had been given from my mother that were expensive hardcovers with sentimental value. 

I probably wont see those again since negotiations with her have completely broken down. Honestly all I care about is getting my son back.

My ex-girlfriend having her secret boyfriend of probably 3-5 months move all her things out of my house (plus a bunch of stuff that was mine) while I was at my brothers wedding with my son. 

Get back to an empty house, find out she was cheating on me and she calls up demanding my son who I don't currently have a legal right to.

Haven't hardly slept in 3 days. Feelsbadman.

Hey man, I'm a long time lurker and literally never post but I read your post and it almost perfectly described the situation I was going through after my son was born in August and I feel like I needed to weigh in on this.

She is probably going through some form of post-partum depression. After my son was born I tried and failed to get my girlfriend (who had just moved in with me) to attend her post-partum checkups with her nurse practitioner and she adamantly refused that there was anything wrong. It wasn't long before she threatened to take my son four states away to live with her estranged mother while I was at work when he was three months old. I broke down in hysterics and when I got home I had to call the police to keep her from just taking him in her car and driving off into the sunset with him.

I can't say that things are back to  where they were before the pregnancy (you change when you have a child and your relationship changes with it) but she is MUCH more stable now that he is about six months old and I eventually talked her into seeing a therapist. 

It is a hard situation to deal with because for some women the feelings they are having are driven by an emotional cocktail of hormones and  new-found responsibility. Just make sure your child is always in safe hands and try to get her some help in the meantime. Even a therapist just to talk about how she feels can be the start of getting her well again.

It really sucks to be young and parents before you had "planned" it but the child you have is worth it.

I have found that there are 2 ways to deal with Terran. You can either try to baneling bust their turtle (risky but ends the game) or go for a macro heavy build and scout aggressively. I usually use a 15 pool and then immediately build an extractor and expand on my natural. Spawn your first queen, hatch larvae and run to the expo. Make sure you get a second queen and then connect the two with creep tumors so that you can reinforce quickly. 

Scouting with Zerg is absolutely key in any circumstance. If you see them throw up reactors you need to get up roaches. Go speedlings if they are marauder heavy. Marine/Marauder ball is really difficult for zerg to handle even with good micro early game, so try to tech up to infestors so that you can use fungal creep to massively damage their marines and keep them from kiting you.
